name: schedule
title: Schedule
description: A day as hours down a rail, each event as tall as it lasts.
use: A day, or a few days side by side, of things booked at a time: meetings, appointments, shifts, talks at a conference. The hours run from --schedule-from to --schedule-to and each event sets --start and --end in hours. Write each event's title and time as text, so the list reads without the drawing.

instead.when: The spans are compared on one shared scale, one row to a thing, such as phases of a project
A month is shown, and a reader picks a day from it
The events are moments in the order they happened, with no length
The events are read as rows of facts and sorted, not placed in time

classes.name: schedule
classes.description: The hours from --schedule-from to --schedule-to, each --schedule-hour tall: a rail of labels at the start, then one column for each day

classes.name: schedule-now
classes.description: Draws an ink line with a dot at --now through the day marked aria-current="date", or through every day when none is, and a hairline through the other days

classes.name: schedule-rail
classes.description: The labels of the hours, one item to an hour from --schedule-from to --schedule-to, each centered on its hairline. Hide it with aria-hidden: the events say their times in words

classes.name: schedule-day
classes.description: One day's column, for several days side by side: an optional schedule-heading over its schedule-events. Mark today with aria-current="date". A schedule of one day may leave it out

classes.name: schedule-heading
classes.description: The name of a day, over its column, in muted ink; today's takes the strong ink

classes.name: schedule-events
classes.description: The events of one day, in order of time, on the scale's hairlines: one at every hour and one down the day's start

classes.name: schedule-event
classes.description: One event from --start to --end, in lane --lane of --lanes: a quiet sheet of tinted ink with a rounded ink bar inside its start, a pixel clear of the hairlines. Put it on the list item, or on a link or a button inside one. A short event keeps one line

classes.name: schedule-title
classes.description: What the event is: one line that ends in an ellipsis

classes.name: schedule-time
classes.description: When it is, written with <time> elements: a quiet line under the title, or beside it in a short event when both fit

states.name: current
states.description: The event in progress, or the one open beside the schedule: an ink sheet

states.name: today
states.description: Today: its heading takes the strong ink and schedule-now draws its line through it

properties.name: --schedule-from
properties.description: The first hour, from 0 to 24; fractions work

properties.name: --schedule-rail
properties.description: The width of the rail of labels

properties.name: --schedule-color
properties.description: The ink the events are tinted and edged with

properties.name: --now
properties.description: The hour of the line of schedule-now, such as 13.5 for half past one

properties.name: --lane
properties.description: Where the event stands among events that overlap it, from 0 at the start; 0 by default

properties.name: --lanes
properties.description: How many events stand side by side where this one does; 1 by default

example:
1. 9 AM
  2. 10 AM
  3. 11 AM
  4. 12 PM

  1. Standup

    9:00 – 9:30

  2. Design review

    10:00 – 11:30
